title: Drag a style over two things and the app counts them at you
goal: Carry a saved colour or a text style over two selected layers and the line under the pointer reads "Paints Fill on all 2 of them with Danger" or "Sets all 2 of them in Heading". That is a machine counting, not a person talking. Two things are both, and the sentence should sound like somebody said it.
notes:
From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-09-text-style-drag.json, which asked for it to be fixed across both places rather than in one and left wrong in the other.

Exact strings, read on 2026-09-09: Sources/PhotonzCore/ColorDrop.swift:206 "Paints \(target.part) on all \(target.reaches) of them with \(colour)" and Sources/PhotonzCore/TextStyleDrop.swift:102 "Sets \(who) in \(style.name)" where who is "all \(target.reaches) of them". Sources/Photonz/EffectsListInspector.swift:382 has a third of the same shape ("Stops it drawing on all N of them"); include it if the extraction reaches, and say so either way.

House copy rules apply: plain short human language, no em dashes.
acceptance: The colour drop and the text style drop both read as plain English for two, and both still name the count for three or more
The two sentences are built from one place rather than fixed twice, so they cannot drift apart again
Existing tests that pin these sentences are updated, and the walk that photographs the drop line still passes
To see it: Scripts/probe-app.sh, select two text layers, and drag a text style tile over them
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
